findings.description: The requirement bounds only the interval between consecutive services while integrity checks run. It does not bound the interval from watchdog activation to the first service or from the last service to the end of start-up; it can also be satisfied without two services. SYS-SUP-015 requires prevention of an independent watchdog reset throughout fault-free start-up.
findings.requested_change: Specify the software obligation that prevents an independent watchdog reset throughout fault-free start-up, including the first and last service intervals.

findings.description: The requirement constrains each window-watchdog refresh but does not require a refresh before the window expires. An implementation making no refresh satisfies the statement even if an enabled watchdog resets during fault-free start-up, contrary to SYS-SUP-015.
findings.requested_change: Specify the software obligation that prevents a window-watchdog reset throughout fault-free start-up, including refresh availability when the watchdog is enabled.

findings.description: The requirement assigns the supervisor software responsibility for holding the outputs low from any reset, including the interval before software configures the pins. CON-SUP-132 assigns the low level during that interval to external pull-down resistors, while the pins are inputs.
findings.requested_change: State the software-controlled portion of the low-output obligation and identify the external pull-down behavior as a hardware dependency.

findings.description: The requirement combines independently verifiable mappings for nine fault codes and multiple entity values. A report can use the correct mapping for one fault class and an incorrect mapping for another.
findings.requested_change: Split the mappings into independently judgeable requirements or reference a controlled mapping table with separately verifiable entries.

findings.description: Retention of the safe-state latch, per-code detection counts and fault history are independently verifiable obligations: any one can be retained across resets while another is lost.
findings.requested_change: Separate the retention obligations for the latch, detection counts and fault history.

findings.description: The requirement places no lower bound on the first refresh after the window watchdog is enabled, so it permits an early refresh that causes a reset during fault-free start-up, contrary to SYS-SUP-015. OP-SWR-001 also identifies this missing first-refresh limit.
findings.requested_change: Require the first refresh after enabling to avoid an early watchdog reset, with any hardware-specific limit resolved from supported evidence.

findings.description: The requirement bounds refresh intervals during start-up but does not bound the interval between the last start-up refresh and the first refresh under SWR-WDG-004. That first normal refresh could occur too early or too late and cause a watchdog reset.
findings.requested_change: Specify the permissible refresh interval across the transition from start-up to normal servicing, consistent with SYS-SUP-012 and SYS-SUP-015.

findings.description: The requirement bounds the interval from enabling to the first refresh and from the last refresh to the end of start-up, but does not define those intervals when start-up ends before any refresh. OP-SWR-001 permits enabling only at the first control cycle, so a start-up with no refresh is a relevant case.
findings.requested_change: Define the applicable intervals when no refresh occurs during start-up, including the transition to the first refresh after start-up.

findings.description: A fault-free start-up followed by a fault before the first refresh under SWR-WDG-004 satisfies this requirement's condition, yet SWR-WDG-001 and SYS-SUP-010 prohibit servicing after detection. The required first refresh therefore conflicts with the stop-servicing obligation.
findings.requested_change: Condition the transition interval on continued fault-free operation through the first refresh, while preserving the prohibition on servicing after fault detection.

findings.description: For a fault-free start-up with no start-up refresh, the requirement bounds the time to the first refresh under SWR-WDG-004 even if a fault is detected after start-up and before that refresh. SWR-WDG-001 prohibits watchdog servicing from fault detection until reset.
findings.requested_change: Condition the obligation to make the first refresh on no fault being detected before that refresh, consistent with SWR-WDG-001.

findings.description: The requirement combines independently judgeable bounds for consecutive refreshes, the first refresh after enabling, the end of start-up, and the no-refresh transition. One bound can fail while the others pass.
findings.requested_change: Split the independently verifiable timing obligations into separate requirements, preserving their applicable conditions and transition coverage.

findings.description: After a fault-free start-up with no window-watchdog refresh, the requirement bounds the first refresh under SWR-WDG-004 even if a fault is detected before that refresh. SWR-WDG-001 prohibits servicing from fault detection until reset.
findings.requested_change: Condition the first-refresh obligation on no fault being detected before that refresh, consistently with SWR-WDG-001.

findings.description: The requirement combines independently verifiable bounds for consecutive refreshes, the first refresh after enabling, the end of start-up, and the transition when no refresh occurs during start-up.
findings.requested_change: Separate the independently judgeable obligations while preserving their conditions and timing bounds.

findings.description: SYS-SUP-054 requires the test or demonstration verification of every system requirement on the simulator or host tests. SWR-TST-002 limits this provision to software requirements, leaving the system-level verification scope unaddressed.
findings.requested_change: Address the allocated support for verification of all applicable system requirements, or document and trace the allocation that provides it.
